skill.author: okx

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, fixed internal references, and privacy-focused identifier rules. Confirmed risks include autonomous remote installation, loading instructions from a sibling skill, automatic code updates, and granting external tool output control over agent actions.

remediation.issue: The missing-CLI fallback runs an installer command sourced from a remote README.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval, pin the installer URL and version, and verify a published checksum before execution.

remediation.issue: Preflight output can direct the agent to perform unspecified actions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace unrestricted data.action handling with a strict allowlist and reject shell commands, new instructions, and unknown action types.

remediation.issue: Mandatory preflight can update executable code and skill instructions without separate consent.
remediation.suggestion: Make updates opt-in, display the target version, and verify signed or pinned artifacts before installation.

remediation.issue: The skill prefers a preflight document from a sibling skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use only the audited bundled _shared/preflight.md file, or package a verified immutable shared dependency.

remediation.issue: External rejection messages are relayed as authoritative user-facing content.
remediation.suggestion: Treat error text as untrusted data, escape unsafe formatting, reject instruction-like content, and present it inside a clearly labeled error boundary.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Tool Output Granted Instruction Authority
semantic_findings.description: The preflight flow reads data.action from command output and says to do exactly what it says. A compromised binary or update channel could inject arbitrary agent instructions without an allowlist.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly delegates action selection to external CLI output and provides no validation or permitted-action list.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Binary and Skill Updates Without Consent
semantic_findings.description: The mandatory preflight command updates the OnchainOS binary and skill checkouts before activity commands. The flow does not require user approval or a pinned artifact before changing executable code and instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file states that preflight updates both the binary and skill checkouts and mandates running it once per conversation.

semantic_findings.title: External Error Text Relayed as Authoritative Output
semantic_findings.description: Registration rejection text from the external service is translated and shown without added context or sanitization. A compromised service could place deceptive or instruction-like content directly in the assistant response.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The flow explicitly treats the returned error field as authoritative and requires displaying its content, while no content validation is specified.

content.user_title: Register an ASP for the OKX.AI Hackathon
content.value_statement: Hackathon registration requires selecting an eligible Trading ASP and the correct competition account. This skill guides confirmation, submission, and result handling through OnchainOS.
actual_capabilities: Explains Trading ASP eligibility, trial, subscription, and funding requirements.
Lists authorized user agents and filters entries with the exact ASP role.
Collects a Web3 account choice or a CeFi account choice with an OKX UID.
Requires explicit confirmation before submitting an irreversible registration.
Submits registration through the OnchainOS CLI or the matching MCP tool.
Handles rejection, service, and validation errors using documented response rules.
limitations: Requires an existing Trading ASP and does not create agent identities.
Requires OnchainOS, wallet login, and access to the user's authorized agent list.
Registration cannot be listed, updated, undone, or checked through this skill.
The skill does not verify account funding before registration.

use_cases.title: Register an Existing Trading ASP
use_cases.description: Select an eligible ASP, confirm its requirements, choose an account, and submit the hackathon registration.

use_cases.title: Check Entry Requirements
use_cases.description: Review eligibility, subscription, free-trial, account, and funding conditions before starting registration.

use_cases.title: Resolve Registration Errors
use_cases.description: Interpret documented rejection, service, login, account-type, address, and UID errors.

prompt_templates.title: Check Eligibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the eligibility requirements for the OKX.AI Trading Hackathon and tell me what I need before registration.

prompt_templates.title: Start Registration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me register one of my existing Trading ASPs for the OKX.AI Trading Hackathon.

prompt_templates.title: Register a CeFi Account
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through registering my existing Trading ASP with a CeFi competition account. Ask for each required confirmation and value.
prompt_templates.scenario: CeFi registration requiring an OKX UID

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failed Submission
prompt_templates.prompt: My hackathon registration failed. Use the returned error code to identify whether this is rejection, service availability, or input validation.

output_examples.input: Can my existing Trading ASP enter the hackathon?
output_examples.output: Yes, if it is a trading-type ASP, offers a subscription service, and includes a three-day free trial. Registration also needs an eligible competition account.

output_examples.input: I want to register with my Web3 account.
output: The skill lists your authorized ASPs and asks you to select one.
It asks you to confirm the ASP requirements and choose the Web3 account.
It submits only after your explicit confirmation.

output_examples.output: The hackathon registration service is currently unavailable. Retry shortly; this result does not indicate an ASP eligibility failure.

best_practices: Use the current authorized agent listing and never guess an agent identifier.
Review every confirmation prompt and submit only after an explicit user reply.
Use a dedicated CeFi sub-account when practical and mask the OKX UID in displayed commands.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to create a new ASP or agent identity.
Do not substitute standard competition registration for hackathon ASP registration.
Do not expose JWTs, raw OKX UIDs, or internal activity identifiers.

faq.question: Can this skill create a Trading ASP?
faq.answer: No. It registers an existing Trading ASP and directs users without one to the creation tutorial.

faq.question: What makes an ASP eligible?
faq.answer: It must be a trading-type ASP with a subscription service and a three-day free trial.

faq.question: Which competition accounts are supported?
faq.answer: The flow supports a Web3 wallet account or a CeFi account that includes an OKX UID.

faq.question: Does registration check my account balance?
faq.answer: No. Registration does not check balance, but the hackathon later expects at least 300 USDT-equivalent assets.

faq.question: Can I undo or update a registration?
faq.answer: No. The documented interface has no list, update, status, or undo operation.

faq.question: How does the skill protect identifiers?
faq.answer: It limits agent ID display, masks the OKX UID in command output, and does not expose the internal activity ID.
